record.original_question: For a preemptive multiprocessor real-time system under global Earliest Deadline First scheduling, determine an exact decision procedure or computational complexity for EDF schedulability of implicit-deadline sporadic task systems. The input is an implicit-deadline sporadic task system tau, in which each task has D_i = T_i, and a positive integer m > 1; the question is whether global EDF meets every deadline for every legal sequence of job arrivals on a platform of m preemptive processors.

evidence.quote: Problem 4 (Exact multiprocessor global EDF-schedulability — implicit-deadline tasks.) Input: Implicit-deadline sporadic task system τ . A positive integer m > 1. Question: Is τ EDF-schedulable upon a platform comprised of m preemptive processors?

Sufficient EDF-schedulability tests are known; for instance, it is known that any implicit-deadline task system τ satisfying U(τ ) ≤ m − (m − 1) × maxτi∈τ{Ci/Ti} is EDF-schedulable on an m-processor platform
It is easy to see that the above condition is not exact

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An implicit-deadline sporadic task system is a finite collection τ = {τ_1, …, τ_n} of tasks. Each task τ_i is described by a pair (C_i, T_i) of positive rationals with C_i ≤ T_i, where T_i is both the minimum inter-arrival separation and the relative deadline (so D_i = T_i), and C_i is the worst-case execution requirement. Such a task generates a (possibly infinite) sequence of jobs; consecutive jobs of τ_i are released at least T_i time units apart, and each job released at time r has an absolute deadline r + T_i and requires up to C_i units of execution before its deadline. The utilization of τ is U(τ) = Σ_i C_i / T_i.

Fix an integer m > 1 and consider a platform of m identical preemptive processors. Global Earliest Deadline First (EDF) scheduling works as follows: at every instant, among all jobs that have been released and are not yet complete, schedule (on the m processors) up to m jobs with the smallest absolute deadlines, breaking ties arbitrarily but consistently; preemption and migration of jobs across processors are allowed at no cost. A job sequence is legal if it respects the sporadic inter-arrival and execution-bound constraints of τ. The system τ is said to be globally EDF-schedulable on m processors if, for every legal sequence of job releases, the global EDF schedule meets every absolute deadline.

Problem. Given as input an implicit-deadline sporadic task system τ and an integer m > 1, determine the exact computational complexity of deciding whether τ is globally EDF-schedulable on m preemptive processors, and in particular exhibit an exact decision procedure for this problem.
artifact.status_search_result: Sufficient (but not exact) utilization-based tests for global EDF on implicit-deadline sporadic tasks have long been known, and general multiprocessor sporadic schedulability has been shown to be PSPACE-hard, but no exact decision procedure of established complexity is known specifically for global EDF schedulability of implicit-deadline sporadic task systems. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Multiprocessor schedulability of arbitrary-deadline sporadic tasks: complexity and antichain algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: Schedulability problem on multiprocessors for sporadic tasks shown to be PSPACE-hard; antichain algorithm proposed but limited in practice.
status_evidence.claim: General multiprocessor sporadic schedulability is computationally hard; no efficient exact test for global EDF is given.

status_evidence.title: Exact Schedulability Test for global-EDF Scheduling of Periodic Hard Real-Time Tasks on Identical Multiprocessors
status_evidence.snippet: Exploits predictability of global-EDF via a feasibility-interval simulation; complexity remains very high.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists via simulation over a feasibility interval, but no efficient exact procedure or tight complexity bound is established.
